taxonomy.note: Accepted by Kew/POWO. The learner remains species-level while preserving accepted infraspecific taxonomy.

evidence: BONAP/NAPA provides a county-level native distribution map for Monarda citriodora and is the project's primary range cross-check.
Hays County — UT Plant Resources Center's Purola Preserve flora explicitly lists M. citriodora among native/naturalized plants that occurred naturally and were not introduced.

Travis County — Harvard University Herbaria specimen GH 01600559 was collected 10 miles northwest of Austin on hills in 1940 and determined as M. citriodora; UT PRC also indexes multiple Travis County specimens.
Comal County — Harvard University Herbaria specimen GH 01600579 was collected west of Landa Park, New Braunfels, on limestone hills in 1946 and determined as M. citriodora.
target_zone_range.guardrail: Lemon beebalm is widely seeded in wildflower plantings, so landscaped/seeded observations are not used to manufacture native counties. The PASS rests on BONAP plus natural-flora/herbarium evidence in three target-zone counties.

morphology.look_here_first: Look at the floral bracts and calyx teeth, not just the purple color: lemon beebalm has conspicuous long bristle tips on the bracts and especially the calyx teeth. The stacked, interrupted flower whorls usually have purplish bracts and white-to-pink/lavender spotted corollas.
diagnostic_traits: erect aromatic annual, usually with a four-angled mint-family stem
leaves opposite; blades usually lanceolate to oblong-lanceolate, with entire to serrate margins
inflorescence an interrupted terminal spike of usually 2–6 dense flower whorls/verticils
upper floral bracts often conspicuously purple or purple-tinted
bracts abruptly narrow to conspicuous bristle-like tips
calyx tubular and strongly ribbed; calyx teeth terminate in long, stiff bristle-like tips
corolla bilabiate, white to pink or lavender/purple, commonly with purple spots or lines on the lower lip
two fertile stamens are held under the curved upper corolla lip
fruit breaks into four small nutlets typical of Lamiaceae

confusers.separator: M. punctata has cream-to-yellow corollas with purple spotting and pale white/pink bracts whose tips are acute or acuminate but not long-bristled; its calyx teeth are short triangular/lanceolate rather than long bristle-tipped.

M. fistulosa usually presents a single dense terminal head (or much less obviously tiered heads) rather than the strongly interrupted stack of whorls typical of M. citriodora; use calyx/bract structure to confirm.

A western/central Texas relative that can resemble M. citriodora. Do not separate on flower color alone; use the regional Monarda key, especially bract and calyx-tooth form, when encountered near the western edge of the project area.

diagnostic_roles: side view of interrupted multi-tier inflorescence
floral bract macro showing purple surface and long bristle tip
calyx macro showing long bristle-tipped teeth
opposite leaf pair and square stem node
photo_verification.provenance_note: Prefer the user's iNaturalist material for study images when it actually shows the required diagnostic structure. Public-reuse licensing must still be verified photo-by-photo before any public distribution.
